the nature of community conflict depends on the type of threat and the social processes that are generated by the threat.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nature of the environmental threat and the type of community social conflict that it generates are related in a complex manner.
rural communities are more vulnerable to environmental conflict when they are not able to mobilize strong ties in response to environmental hazards.
rural communities are likely to be more cohesive and have a greater capacity to mobilize in response to facility siting disputes than in response to toxic contamination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the type of conflict occurring in a community depends on the social and ecological processes at play in that community.
community conflict is not inevitable in either siting or contamination cases.
the social process that unfolds around the presence or absence and the perception of a hazard agent is a critical factor in the type of social conflict that occurs.
